game: LA @ JAX, Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-19 09:30 ET, outdoors (home JAX). Closing line only: JAX +3, total 44.5. Open, rest, travel not in pack.

script.base: Market prices a close game, not a blowout: LA is a 3-point favorite (spread is 3.0, so the 3.5+ dog-throws-more rule does not auto-trigger) with implied totals LA 23.8 and JAX 20.8 on a 44.5 outdoor total. LA is without WR Puka Nacua (30 targets, 283 yards, 331 air yards in weeks 4-6) and RT Rob Havenstein, and Stafford's EPA/dropback is already -0.02 when blitzed vs 0.27 when not, against a JAX blitz rate of 29%. Base flow is a one-score game in which Kyren Williams keeps the lead-back carries (40 carries, 192 rush yards in those three weeks vs Blake Corum 15/57) and also the checkdowns, while JAX stays balanced around Travis Etienne (43/200) with Trevor Lawrence as a runner (16/76) and Brian Thomas Jr. as the WR1 (23 targets, 219 yards).
script.flip1: LA leads by two scores early, clocks it with Kyren, and starter pass volume stalls: Davante Adams and Brian Thomas yardage undershoot, and Etienne's rush line dies if Jacksonville abandons the run.
script.flip2: Havenstein wrecks LA rush efficiency or JAX grabs the lead, so Kyren's carries fall and the game becomes Stafford checkdowns plus Lawrence throwing to Thomas. The other flip is an outdoor slog: weather is not saved, and a wind or rain drag on a 44.5 would knock every yardage over down together.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse report: LA WR Puka Nacua Out (ankle), LA T Rob Havenstein Out (ankle), JAX LB Devin Lloyd Out (calf), JAX TE Quintin Morris Out (groin). Nacua's 10 targets a game leave the tree; weeks 4-6 shares with him active were Adams 26/183/335, Kyren 16/120/70, Higbee 9/65/70, Whittington 8/63/44, Atwell 6/160/159, Corum 6/-5/16. No prior game with Nacua sitting is in the pack, so next-man share is not measured. Havenstein out is an OL hit: rush efficiency down, more quick throws, deep WR yards down. That helps Kyren, Higbee and short-area Whittington (44 air yards on 8 targets) and hurts Adams, whose 335 air yards produced only 183 receiving yards (7.0 yards per target). Lloyd out is the defensive leak for RB, TE and slot. Morris is not on the weeks 4-6 target list, so his absence does not reprice Brenton Strange (8 targets, 67 yards). Passed, not bet: Adams over 56.5 (downfield profile loses to the blitz/OL script; JAX blitz 29% is exactly where Stafford is negative), Whittington over 15.5 (depth, last-4 includes 7 and 7, four mouths for Nacua's targets, no without-Nacua share), Higbee over 31.5 (stand-in sits above a 21.7 yards-per-game weeks 4-6 role; last-4 37, 0, 25, 40).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Havenstein's absence did what the 50-rush game already did: Kyren was in the 50s on the ground, Corum took the third-down catches he already had a 6-target toehold on, and the receiving day stayed in the 30s, so rush-plus-rec finished under 90.5 the way 87 did. On the other leg LA never let Thomas see the left side, played the right-side 5.15 YPA split, and a quiet outdoor morning (forecast was not in the file) plus Etienne and Lawrence carries (43 and 16 in weeks 4-6) held Thomas on a 49-yard afternoon. The 44.5 close and a 3-point spread never forced the pass volume the lean needed. That counter is strong enough to keep Thomas a lean and to flag Kyren for size, not strong enough to erase Kyren's target, linebacker and recent-role stack.
slip_story: One story only: a close 23.8-20.8 game, not a shootout and not a blowout. LA without Nacua checks down and still hands to Kyren against a 4.34 YPC front missing Lloyd, so rush-plus-rec is the anchor. Thomas over belongs only as the same-script JAX WR1 leg, because a 3-point dog in a game LA will blitz does not have to abandon him. Do not add Adams over (needs the downfield shots this pressure script kills), Whittington or Higbee (same checkdowns Kyren already owns, worse floors), Etienne under (needs JAX to quit the run, which +3 does not promise, and LA has allowed 16 runs of 10+), or a total under with these overs. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player, no depth receiver.
